summary: Tenant-wide 429s during nightly backup: CDN preflight + SDK connection reuse causing token double-counting
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported repeated 429 throttles across their tenant coinciding with their nightly snapshot export job (00:30 - 01:15 UTC). Impact: large portion of ingest and generation requests returning 429 for ~45 minutes, causing downstream job failures and missed backups.

Initial impact assessment suggests tenant token accounting was exhausted quickly despite average traffic being within provisioned committed capacity. Customer observed many short-lived connections and parallel preflight/health probes toward the API endpoint during the window.

Impact: Failed snapshot export (partial), multiple client retries, 60+ incident alerts in customer's monitoring during the window. No data loss reported; jobs retried next day but delayed.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy SDK v2.3.0 with default connection pool settings (keepalive enabled) in a multi-worker scheduled job.
2) Configure backup job to open 40 parallel workers that each open websocket/HTTP2 connections and perform preflight/metadata checks before uploading chunked export files.
3) Schedule job to all start within same minute.
4) Observe rate-limiter metrics and token accounting in API gateway during the ramp.

Observed: preflight/health probes and SDK reconnects generate short-lived sessions that increment tenant token counters; HTTP/2 connection reuse combined with CDN edge preflight behavior led to double-counting of some requests in rate accounting layer.
logs:
Sample from api-gateway logs (trimmed):
[2026-03-10T00:31:12Z] tenant=storebound request_id=abc123 path=/v1/upload status=429 token_bucket_remaining=0 refill_window=60s
[2026-03-10T00:31:12Z] tenant=storebound src=cdn-edge preflight=true conn_id=xyz998 increment=1
[2026-03-10T00:31:12Z] tenant=storebound src=origin keepalive_reused=true conn_id=xyz998 increment=1
--
Rate limiter metrics snapshot: tenant_tokens_allocated=500k tenant_tokens_consumed=505k (spike during export ramp)
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 00:30 UTC: Customer job starts (40 workers).
- 00:31 UTC: Spike in short-lived preflight/metadata requests from CDN edges + SDK reconnects.
- 00:31-01:15 UTC: Sustained token drain and 429s.
- 01:20 UTC: Autoscaling burst and token refill mitigated, errors subside.

Hypotheses tested:
- H1: Misconfigured tenant quota - rejected (quota matches committed plan).
- H2: Health probes / CDN preflight double-counting - supported by correlated conn_id increments in logs.
- H3: SDK v2 connection reuse causing duplicate accounting when requests traverse CDN and origin - reproduced in staging with synthetic worker burst.

Findings: When a client establishes an HTTP/2 connection that is proxied through CDN edges, the gateway's rate-accounting observed both the edge preflight handshake and the origin reuse as separate token events in ~12% of sampled flows. SDK behavior that aggressively opened and closed connections for each worker amplified the effect.
comments: 2026-03-10 03:15 - Aisha Khan (Support): Notified SRE after customer provided initial logs and their job schedule. Customer temporarily staggered retries which reduced the peak, but 429s continued until token refill window completed.

2026-03-10 05:02 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced in staging by running 50 parallel worker processes using SDK v2.3.0 against a prod-like gateway. Observed double increment pattern for conn_id when proxied via our CDN testbed. Opened INT-10245 to track root-cause change in gateway accounting logic.

2026-03-11 09:40 - Customer (StoreBound): Confirmed they use CDN fronting and scheduled jobs that kick off at the same time across many instances. Asked for short-term workaround to avoid nightly failures.

2026-03-12 11:12 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Implemented temporary rule to ignore preflight probes from known CDN user-agent string for token accounting; applied to storebound tenant as experiment. Errors dropped by ~90% in controlled replay.
workaround:
Short-term: Customer staggered worker start times by 5s and reduced parallelism from 40 -> 10 per region; we applied an edge-filter on preflight UA to exclude known CDN probe patterns from token accounting for this tenant. This reduced 429s immediately.
Medium-term: Advise customer to upgrade to SDK v2.3.2 (patch forthcoming) which reduces aggressive connect/reconnect behavior and exposes an option to reuse long-lived connections across workers.
resolution:
Planned final fix: Change gateway accounting to dedupe proximal preflight/origin pairs when connection metadata (conn_id, tcp_tuple) indicate same logical request path. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/13478 (WIP).
Customer follow-ups: update backup scheduler to stagger starts; upgrade SDK when patch released.
Status: Mitigation applied (edge UA filter) and customer advised. Engineering to deploy accounting fix behind feature flag for selected tenants for controlled rollout.
